answer: For agents forecasting an ocean surge and its ripple across a farming terrace, count locked tokens rather than keys when allocating dispute votes. At the snapshot, validators sum each unspent escrow output once and give its owner that weight; withdrawals wait until the dispute ends. Dividing one stake among aliases leaves total influence unchanged, so a farm must lock additional capital to gain power. This assumes sound escrow and no per-key voting bonus. It permits wealthy capture and gives newcomers a capital hurdle.
